title: introduce-cycle-accurate-kvlat-probe-and-scheduler-snapshotter-with-replay-driver
author: Ravi Menon
description:
Motivation: We need a lower-noise, high-fidelity instrumentation for KV-cache and scheduler interactions to diagnose subtle latency spikes observed in production request tail latency (ENG-482). This PR adds a cycle-accurate KV-latency probe, a lightweight scheduler snapshotter that captures in-flight batch metadata at key scheduling points, and a small, replayable microdriver to run deterministic microbench workloads and export timeline traces. The intent is not to become a full profiler but to provide reproducible microbench artifacts for root cause analysis and perf regressions.

Design overview: single, consistent probe API (kv::CycleProbe) exposed as RAII ranges that record CPU cycle deltas and optional NVTX ranges when enabled. A scheduler::Snapshotter captures a compact snapshot (batch id, batch shape, queue depth, priority tag, kv-prefix-hits) at enqueue/dequeue/dispatch boundaries and emits a compact protobuf line to the microdriver trace sink. The replayable driver (tools/perf/replay_driver) can feed recorded traces into the runtime with time-control to reproduce scheduling interactions. To keep overhead minimal, cycle counters and events are aggregated to per-thread ring buffers and flushed asynchronously to avoid mutating hot paths.

What this PR changes (high level):
- Adds kv/CycleProbe implementation (C++), header, and unit tests.
- Adds scheduler/Snapshotter and light-weight ring buffer util.
- Adds replay_driver binary under tools/perf/ with a mode to ingest recorded traces and run deterministic workloads.
- Adds a perf dashboard exporter script to convert output traces into a short JSON summary and speedscope-compatible timeline.
- Updates runtime config flags to enable/disable probes at runtime and a small README explaining usage.

Checklist (implemented): 
- [x] Low-overhead cycle probe API with opt-in NVTX integration
- [x] Scheduler snapshot points at enqueue/dequeue/dispatch
- [x] Replay driver able to feed traces with controlled timing
- [x] Unit tests for probe correctness and ring buffer semantics
- [x] Example recorded trace used by CI microbench to validate no regression in throughput

Testing and metrics: I added a deterministic microbench that runs one synthetic model with configurable batch shapes. On our internal perf infra the new driver reproduced a 14% tail increase associated with a rare kv-prefix-miss interleaving; with a scheduler config change we verified a 9% improvement. End-to-end CI includes a smoke run of the replay driver. Local perf: overhead of CycleProbe in busy loops was measured at ~1.3% median and ~2.7% p95 when NVTX is disabled; NVTX-on increases overhead by ~6% and is off by default.

How to run: 
1) Build: ninja tools/perf/replay_driver
2) Record trace (dev): export REDWOOD_PROBE_ENABLE=1; run minimal microbench with --trace-out=trace.pb
3) Replay: tools/perf/replay_driver --replay trace.pb --speed-factor 1.0 --export speedscope.json

Related work: this complements earlier NVTX and counters work (see ENG-513) but focuses on deterministic replay and cycle-accurate KV latencies to make scheduler interactions reproducible. This intentionally keeps trace payloads small to avoid perturbing the runtime during capture.

Notes for reviewers: pay special attention to the ring buffer memory model (lock-free single-producer single-consumer) and the atomic sequence handling in Snapshotter. I left NVTX integration behind a runtime flag to reduce noise in production.

release_notes: Added an opt-in cycle-accurate KV-latency probe and scheduler snapshotter plus a replayable microdriver and exporter for deterministic perf debugging. These are opt-in observability primitives for internal use and do not change runtime behavior when disabled.
